MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  NOVEMBER 14, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at
7:09 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Representatives from the McNulty School of Irish Dance led the audience in the Pledge of
Allegiance and performed a dance for the audience.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman.

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  A RESOLUTION OF COMMENDATION OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  COMMENDING VESTAR FOR ITS REVITALIZATION OF PENINSULA SHOPPING
  CENTER IN ROLLING HILLS ESTATES

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN presented a Resolution of Commendation to Vestar for its
  revitalization of the Peninsula Shopping Center. Jeff Axtell accepted the
  commendation on behalf of Vestar and thanked the City Council, staff and the
  tenants for their support.

B.  A PROCLAMATION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES SUPPORTING ENERGY UPGRADE CALIFORNIA’S “DO YOUR THING”
  INITIATIVE

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN issued a proclamation in support of Energy Upgrade
  California’s “Do Your Thing” Initiative.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
NOVEMBER 14, 2017
 5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 24, 2017 (WORKSHOP)

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 24,
  2017 (WORKSHOP) AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 24, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 24, 2017 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

C.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 2, 2017 (WORKSHOP)

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 2,
  2017(WORKSHOP) AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – OCTOBER AND NOVEMBER, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 59154 THROUGH 59202 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $409,627.08; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 100117 THROUGH 100717;
  58987 (VOID); 59035 THROUGH 59066; 59117 THROUGH 59140 IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $248,036.07 FOR A GRAND TOTAL OF $657,663.15 WITH
  PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
  consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless
  good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be
  considered under New Business.)

  NONE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
NOVEMBER 14, 2017
 7.  AUDIENCE  ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

  NONE

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

  NONE

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 6, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER  ZUCKERMAN  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  MITCHELL.

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE  THE  PLANNING  COMMISSION  MINUTES  OF
  NOVEMBER 6, 2017.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN’S request for further explanation on
  the two items related to signs, Planning Director Wahba explained that the request to
  amend the Master Program for 550 Deep Valley Drive was submitted for aesthetic
  changes to the signs in the entire area as part of an effort to re-brand the Promenade
  on the Peninsula. With regard to the request to amend the Master Program for Town
  & Country Shopping Center, Planning Director Wahba explained that the signs are
  consistent with the existing signage but designed to provide greater differentiation to
  the Rolling Hills Dental Group as a satellite tenant versus the in-line tenants.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA PROPOSED FORMAT CHANGES

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the report and provide further
  direction to staff if additional agenda changes are requested.

  City Clerk Luce provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT ON THE PROPOSED AGENDA FORMAT
  CHANGES AND PROCEED WITH THE CHANGES BEGINNING IN 2018.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
NOVEMBER 14, 2017
 10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT
  WITH THE CITY MANAGER

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the first amendment to the amended
  and restated employment agreement with the City Manager.

  Mayor Zerunyan reported that the City Council met in closed session on October 24,
  2017 to discuss this matter and this item is on the agenda for approval of the
  amendment.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE THE FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED
  EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT WITH THE CITY MANAGER

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

B.  LED STREETLIGHT REPLACEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve retrofitting all City-owned streetlights
  to LED lamps in the amount of $28,045 under current contract with Siemens, with a
  Southern California Edison incentive of $10,327 for a net cost to the City in the
  amount of $17,718.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material) as
  well as an overview and cost breakdown of the project.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF inquired as to the possibly of requesting that Southern
  California Edison provide an extension given to the incentive program so that the City
  can take advantage of the incentives. Following brief discussion, it was noted that
  extending the program is not an option and many other cities are in a similar
  situation.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Assistant City Manager Grammer
  commented that this project will be undertaken by the City’s signal maintenance
  contractor, Siemens.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE RETROFITTING ALL CITY-OWNED STREETLIGHTS TO LED
  LAMPS IN THE AMOUNT OF $28,045 UNDER CURRENT CONTRACT WITH
  SIEMENS, WITH A SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON INCENTIVE OF $10,327
  FOR A NET COST TO THE CITY IN THE AMOUNT OF $17,718.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
NOVEMBER 14, 2017
 11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  City Attorney Davis reported that staff is preparing DRAFT regulations for the City
  Council’s consideration pertaining to use, cultivation and sale of recreational
  marijuana consistent with the City’s regulations pertaining to medicinal uses.

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information
  and reports to other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or
  activities of currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and their
  various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an interest,
  which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF OCTOBER 23, 2017 – COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF OCTOBER
  23, 2017.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN’S inquiry regarding the discussion
  pertaining to an expenditure for camera coverage at Ernie Howlett Park, COUNCIL
  MEMBER SCHMITZ explained that it was simply a discussion, with no
  recommendation, as it has been reported that certain trainers are misusing the arena.
  Administrative Services Director further explained that staff is still in the process of
  pursuing Wi-Fi/camera options for the parks and other public locations.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

OTHER REPORTS:

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reported that the Neighborhood Watch group met last week with the
primary discussion revolving around emergency preparedness and neighborhood
communication, including radio communication.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported that he attended the LACCE board meeting
noting that the JPA was amended and approximately six additional cities have joined.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported that he attended the West Vector Control District
Board meeting and it was reported there were more West Nile Virus deaths in LA County this
year compared to last year but there have been no reports of the Zika virus.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL reported that she attended the SCAG Southern California
Economic Summit where the main topic was the need to address California’s housing
shortage and the new State regulations regarding housing. She further reported that cities
were also encouraged to consider housing needs during the General Plan Update. Brief
discussion ensued concerning the City’s Housing Element Update. Following brief

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
NOVEMBER 14, 2017
 discussion, staff was directed to provide a report to the City Council on the steps that the
City has taken to address housing needs in the City.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ reported that the PV Transit board met and appointed a
finance subcommittee consisting of her, Council Member Duhovic from Rancho Palos Verdes
and Martin Gombert to review PV Transit revenues and expenditures.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF congratulated COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL on  her
reappointment as the regional representative to the Southern California AQMD Board.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF also noted that the Prepared Peninsula Expo held on October 29
was very well attended and thanked Assistant to the City Manager Davis for her efforts.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL expressed concern regarding the direction the City
Celebration is going and suggested that the matter be discussed by the Equestrian
Committee and at the Policy Development Session. Brief discussion ensued concerning the
challenges facing the event. The City Council concurred that the matters should be
discussed at the Policy Development Session.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members of the
  City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or issues of public
  concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration and/or make
  announcements of interest to the public.

A.  COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE TERMS

  Recommendation: That that the City Council: 1) Make a determination on a case by
  case basis as to the reappointment of current Commissioners and Committee
  Members whose terms expire December 31, 2017; 2) Direct staff to schedule
  interviews and/or conduct recruitment as necessary based on actions taken under
  Recommendation 1; and 3) Direct staff to conduct recruitment for any vacancies
  created by any retiring Committee Member(s).

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO REAPPOINT ALL COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE MEMBERS WHO’S
  TERMS ARE EXPIRING; DIRECTED STAFF TO BEGIN RECRUITMENT AND
  SCHEDULE INTERVIEWS FOR ANY VACANCIES AND; DIRECTED STAFF TO
  SCHEDULE AN INTERVIEW/DISCUSSION WITH THE CHAIR OF EACH
  COMMISSION  AS  WELL  AS  SOLICIT  COMMENTS  FROM  THE
  COMMISSION/COMMITTEE MEMBERS.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  AUTHORIZATION TO ATTEND THE CALIFORNIA CONTRACT CITIES LEGISLATIVE
  TOUR – JANUARY 8-10, 2018

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN reported that the California Contract Cities Legislative Tour is
  scheduled for January 8-10, 2018 in Sacramento and inquired as to the City Council’s
  interest in attending. All Council Members were authorized to attend.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
NOVEMBER 14, 2017
 C.  WASTE MANAGEMENT CONTRACT NEGOTIATION UPDATE – MAYOR ZERUNYAN
  AND COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ (VERBAL REPORT)

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided an update on the Waste Management
  contract negotiation stating that the process has been very productive and included
  input from the equestrian community. She reviewed several minor proposed
  modifications to the contract and stated that the revised contract will be brought to
  the City Council in January or early February.

  Discussion ensued concerning options for addressing organic waste issues and
  reducing landfill waste.

14.  CLOSED SESSION

  NONE

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:49 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the City Council meeting to the next
  regular meeting of the City Council scheduled for Tuesday, November 28, 2017
  beginning at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045
  Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
NOVEMBER 14, 2017
